action.label: It acts with rights: it reads from or writes to an external system (Jira, an API), or it delivers (build, tag, publication, deployment).

limit.label: It bounds what the agent is allowed to do: tools, commands, files, network, secrets.

rule.label: It requires something of the result: “every route has a test”, “no secret in the code”.

compute.label: It produces a result entirely determined by its inputs: next version, files touched, collected facts.

judgment.label: It chooses, interprets, writes or converses: no answer is right in advance.

procedure.label: It chains steps for one type of task.

knowledge.label: It is a fact or a convention the agent must know.

access.text: What does it do with those rights?

consult.label: The agent reads an external system during its work: ticket, documentation page, internal API.

write.label: The agent writes to an external system during its work: comment on a ticket, post a message, create a page.

deliver.label: It builds, tags, publishes or deploys: a shared resource changes.

bypass_limit.text: Who must not be able to override it?

agent.label: The agent alone: a developer may do it by hand without it being an incident.

dev.label: Nobody in the repository, developers included.

team.label: No team: the organisation imposes it on every repository.

incident.text: If the result does not respect it, what does it cost?

yes.label: An incident: shipped bug, vulnerability, non-compliance.

forget.label: Lost time, not an incident; but it must not be possible to forget it.

no.label: Nothing measurable: it is a preference, a style.

checkable.text: Can a program check it, with the same answer every time?

yes.label: Yes: a test, a linter, a command that fails.

bypass_rule.text: Who must not be able to deliver without respecting it?

agent.label: The agent alone: it must notice before handing back.

dev.label: Nobody in the repository: nothing merges without it.

release.label: Nobody in the repository, and it is at delivery that it counts: nothing is published or deployed without it.

team.label: No team: the organisation imposes it on every repository.

on_demand.label: When the agent or a human needs it.

agent_loop.label: At a fixed point in the agent's work: before a tool, after an edit, on stop.

repo_event.label: On a repository event: PR, push, schedule.

isolation.text: Does this work need to be separated from the session?

none.label: No: it relies on what the session already knows.

context.label: It reads a lot (exploration, logs) and would clutter the session's context.

independence.label: It must judge without the author's bias: review, evaluation.

rights.label: It needs different rights from the session, usually fewer: read-only.

parallel.label: Several independent parts can progress at the same time.

scope.text: When does the agent need it?

always.label: On every task in this repository, and it cannot find it alone.

zone.label: Only when it works in a folder or on a type of file.

reference.label: From time to time, for a precise question.

discoverable.label: It never needs to be told: it finds it by reading the repository (manifest, Makefile, tree).

mcp.name: MCP server
mcp.where: An MCP server declared for the repository; its rights (read-only, or writing bounded to one project or one channel) are set on the server's account, not in a prompt.
mcp.why: A right held by the server holds whatever the prompt. What the agent reads there is data, not an instruction: a ticket can carry an injection.
mcp.also: A deny permission on the server's write tools, as a second curtain.

pipeline.name: Delivery workflow
pipeline.where: A CI workflow or pipeline with a plan mode (dry-run) and a protected environment; the agent triggers it through a CLI subcommand, never through the API directly.
pipeline.why: What changes a shared resource runs with audited rights, off the agent's machine, with a human stop point before the irreversible.

permission.name: Agent permission
permission.where: permissions.deny (or ask) in the repository's shared settings (.claude/settings.json), and a PreToolUse hook if the rule depends on the content of the command.
permission.why: The agent's runtime applies it on every tool call; a sentence in AGENTS.md can be forgotten or worked around.
permission.also: Also deny the agent writing to its own settings, otherwise it can lift the rule.

server_protection.name: Server-side protection
server_protection.where: Branch protection, ruleset, protected environment or account rights, on the forge.
server_protection.why: A hook or a local permission can be bypassed by hand (--no-verify, another tool); the server refuses for everyone.
server_protection.also: The same rule as a deny permission, so that the agent does not even try.

managed.name: Organisation managed settings
managed.where: Managed settings for the agent; rulesets and required workflows at organisation level for the forge.
managed.why: A file in the repository can be changed by the team; a managed setting overrides every other level and cannot be removed from the repository.

hook_check.name: Check run by a hook
hook_check.where: A CLI subcommand, a linter or a test, called by an agent hook: before the tool or command it conditions, after an edit, or on stop. It fails with a message that says what to fix.
hook_check.why: The agent cannot forget it. A human can skip it: that is acceptable here, since only the agent forgetting is at stake.

ci_check.name: Blocking CI check
ci_check.where: A CLI subcommand, a linter or an architecture test, made mandatory by branch protection; AGENTS.md can cite it in one line with “Enforced by”.
ci_check.why: Only a required check prevents the merge, whatever the tool and the person. A job in continue-on-error, a path filter that does not trigger it, or a local hook guarantees nothing.
ci_check.also: The same check run by a hook, so that the agent sees it before opening the PR.

release_gate.name: Blocking step of the delivery workflow
release_gate.where: A step of the delivery workflow that calls the check (CLI subcommand, script) and fails before the first irreversible action.
release_gate.why: What is judged at publication cannot be seen at merge: a changelog entry, a version, a signed artifact. The delivery workflow is the only mandatory passage.
release_gate.also: The same check as a PR check, when it can already be done at merge.

org_check.name: Check imposed by the organisation
org_check.where: The same check, as a required workflow or ruleset at organisation level.
org_check.why: A team can neither disable nor weaken it from its repository.

judge.name: Judge and human review
judge.where: A subagent or a judge in CI that flags, a human review that decides; a line in AGENTS.md if the agent must aim for it.
judge.why: A judgment cannot be checked reproducibly: no code guarantees it. Split first: the measurable part (a section present, a link to the ticket) goes back through the grid as a checkable rule.

cli.name: Tested CLI subcommand
cli.where: A subcommand of the repository's CLI (a script if it is truly isolated), with its tests and a JSON output; the skill calls it.
cli.why: A computation written in a prompt is redone every time, and sometimes wrongly; in code, it gives the same result to the agent, the human and CI.

hook_compute.name: Subcommand called by a hook
hook_compute.where: The CLI subcommand, wired to the agent event (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) in the repository's shared settings.
hook_compute.why: A fixed point of the loop is held by the agent's runtime, not by an instruction it must remember.

workflow.name: Repository workflow
workflow.where: A workflow triggered by the event (PR, push, schedule) that calls the CLI subcommand.
workflow.why: A repository event happens even when no agent is running.

session.name: Agent judgment, in the skill
session.where: No dedicated file: the skill that tells the procedure says where the agent decides, between which options, and the CLI provides those options.
session.why: Judging is the agent's job; isolating it without need costs context and round trips.

subagent.name: Subagent
subagent.where: A subagent (.claude/agents/<name>.md) with restricted tools, that returns a structured result.
subagent.why: A subagent starts from a blank context, with its own tools: that is what gives it an independent eye, narrower rights, room to read a lot, or the ability to run in parallel. Without one of these needs, it is a skill.

skill.name: Skill
skill.where: .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, loaded on demand, with its references in references/.
skill.why: A procedure only serves its type of task; loaded in every session, it would cost context everywhere. Each mandatory step of the procedure is a separate piece (rule or computation) that the skill calls.

agents_md.name: A line in AGENTS.md
agents_md.where: AGENTS.md, one line with its why and its date; “Enforced by” if a guardrail carries it.
agents_md.why: AGENTS.md is loaded in every session: only what serves every task and what the agent cannot find alone goes in.

agents_md_zone.name: Folder AGENTS.md
agents_md_zone.where: An AGENTS.md in the folder concerned, or a per-path rule of the tool.
agents_md_zone.why: It is only loaded when the agent works in that zone: the rest of the repository does not pay its cost.

doc.name: Document read on demand
doc.where: A file in docs/agents/, pointed to from AGENTS.md or from the skill that needs it.
doc.why: Reference material loaded in every session drowns the instructions; pointed to, it is only read when it serves.

nothing.name: Nothing to write
nothing.why: What the agent finds by reading the repository does not change what it does; writing it costs context in every session and goes stale.

skippable_condition.name: A condition that can be skipped
skippable_condition.definition: Something the result must respect is written as a sentence. Nothing stops the agent, or a person, from going on without it: a program could check it, with the same answer every time.

determinism.name: A determinism problem
determinism.definition: A result entirely fixed by its inputs is left to the model, which works it out again on every run and sometimes gets it wrong. In code, it gives the same answer to the agent, to a person and to the CI.

limit_only_asked.name: A limit that is only asked for
limit_only_asked.definition: What the agent must not do is written as a request. A sentence can be forgotten or worked around; a permission or a protection refuses whatever the prompt says.

unguarded_action.name: An action without a guard
unguarded_action.definition: The text has the agent read, write or deliver outside the repository with whatever rights the session holds. Nothing bounds those rights, and nothing stops before the irreversible.

weak_guard.name: A guard that can be bypassed
weak_guard.definition: A real guard exists, but not where it counts: someone it should hold can still go around it.

frozen_judgment.name: Judgement frozen in code
frozen_judgment.definition: A choice with no right answer in advance, or a plain convention, is hard-coded. It becomes rigid, and the team ends up working around it.

tidy_helper.name: A helper that only looks tidy
tidy_helper.definition: A separate agent does work that needs no fresh context, no independent eye, no narrower rights and no parallelism. It costs context and round trips for nothing.

dead_weight.name: Dead weight
dead_weight.definition: The agent finds this alone by reading the repository. Writing it costs context in every session and goes stale.

wrong_place.name: Not in the right place
wrong_place.definition: The right kind of thing, held in the wrong file or at the wrong reach: loaded when it does not serve, or missing when it does.

two_in_one.name: Two things in one
two_in_one.definition: One text carries its procedure and other things that are not procedure. Each of them is listed under its own heading; cut them out, and the procedure calls them.
